prompt:
Create one original transparent sprite component sheet for ASHVEIL, our own muted post-apocalyptic pixel-art RPG. This request is for CLOTHING OBJECTS ONLY: eight separate opaque sewn trouser-leg fabric modules, with no wearer. Use the two supplied own clothed worker sheets only as references for their weathered textile palette and crisp detailed sprite rendering. Do not copy the characters or apron. New garment design: sturdy fully opaque ash-brown/grey woven work cloth, fine visible stitches, restrained darker seam piping, modest knee creases, dusty fabric wear, neatly finished edges. Cloth, not skin or leather armor.

Exact layout: TWO COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS, eight complete isolated garment objects. One facing per row. Top row FRONT: anatomical LEFT trouser module in column1, anatomical RIGHT trouser module in column2. Row2 LEFT SIDE: anatomical LEFT module (outer side) then anatomical RIGHT module (inner side). Row3 RIGHT SIDE: anatomical LEFT module (inner side) then anatomical RIGHT module (outer side). Bottom row BACK: anatomical LEFT module then anatomical RIGHT module. These are eight separately drawn views, not one cut-out pair of pants or a full garment spanning two columns. Front views show the gently reinforced front knee cloth; back views show looser rear knee folds and the different back seam construction, not another front view. Left-facing side views face screen-left and right-facing views face screen-right. The outer-side vertical seam is clear on the outer modules; inner-side views have an understated inseam. Opposite anatomical sides must remain separately owned objects.

Each single object is just ONE unfilled, sewn trouser-leg cloth sleeve from an independent upper-thigh overlap cuff down to a hem just below the knee. The top is a short, flat finished cloth overlap cuff, not a waistband. The lower end is a finished fabric hem. All fabric surfaces are opaque, including dark folded inner fabric at edges; only the space outside each garment is transparent. The long central garment is a continuous cloth surface, NOT a shaped anatomical body segment. No circular flesh-colored knee ends, no joint pins, no exposed filling. Do not add a waist, belt, pelvis, fly, crotch, seat bridge, second attached leg, boots, feet, mannequin, person, body, hands, head, props, detached hardware, labels, arrows, or text. No painted shadows, background, ground pad, glow, fog, or checkerboard.

Consistent modest low top-down game-sprite view and identical garment model/material/length across all eight objects. Hang each module vertically in a relaxed near-straight shape with a small cloth bend at the knee. The left/right side orientation is expressed by the garment's bend and seam surfaces. Preserve all the upper cuff, both side contours, knee fabric, and complete lower hem. No long coat tails or loose neighboring cloth. Keep each object within the central 45% of its column width and 65% of its row height, with generous completely transparent space around every object and between all eight cells. Do not connect neighboring modules or crop any edge. Aim for a visually coherent detailed material sprite that remains legible when displayed about 4 to 5 game-world pixels wide and 8 to 11 pixels long; do not bake in a fixed wearer scale. Deliver only the transparent original PNG sheet.
